prompt: Build Kanban Board, a personal task board that runs as one self-contained HTML page with no server, no build step and no libraries. A tab bar across the top switches between sixteen views, one per feature. Columns: create, rename and delete columns, in a fixed order, with a blank or duplicate name refused. Cards: add, edit and delete cards with a title, description, tags, due date and assignee, with an invalid card refused with a message per rule. Move: move a card to any column at any position, or reorder it inside its column. WIP limit: a per-column limit that refuses a move which would overfill the column and says why. Labels: the tag palette, with a filter by tag. Search: filter cards by title or description as you type. Due: overdue, due soon (within three days) and later, relative to today. Sort column: order one column by due date, title or creation date, either direction, without touching the others. Archive: archive a card off the board and restore it. History: undo and redo every board change, twenty steps deep, with a new change discarding the redo branch. Swimlanes: the board grouped by assignee. Assignees: assign and unassign people, and a workload count per person. Export: the board as JSON and as Markdown checklists. Import: paste JSON and add its columns and cards, with every invalid card listed and the valid ones kept. Metrics: cycle time per finished card, the average, and weekly throughput. Persist: the board saved to localStorage under a versioned schema, restored on load, with an older version-1 document migrated.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: kanban-board.html, one self-contained HTML page. All 18 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The page starts with <!doctype html>, makes zero external requests, holds a <nav> with one button[data-tab=NAME] and one <section id="panel-NAME"> per feature, and one plain <script id="app"> (not a module) that runs to completion in node with document, window and localStorage stubbed and leaves window.App.features holding one entry per feature, each with a `model` object of pure functions and a `render(root, state)` function. Sixteen feature tests, one per feature, call the model functions listed in the contract with fixed data and check exact results: new arrays, never mutated inputs; ids unique; board order preserved; archived cards left out of the board, the lanes, the workload and the Markdown export; a WIP refusal that carries a reason; an undo stack capped at twenty with the redo branch cleared by a new change; a version-1 document migrated to version 2 with one column per status in order of first appearance.
contract: Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>, saved as kanban-board.html. Structure: 1. <head> with a <style> holding every rule; no external stylesheet. 2. <body> with a <nav id="tabs"> holding one <button data-tab="NAME"> per feature and a <main> holding one empty <section id="panel-NAME" class="panel"> per feature, in this order: columns, cards, move, wiplimit, labels, search, due, sortcolumn, archive, history, swimlanes, assignees, exporter, importer, metrics, persist. 3. One plain <script id="app"> (no type="module", no import or export) that builds a global `App` and ends with `window.App = App`. It must touch no DOM element and read no user data at load time: the gate extracts this script alone, stubs document, window, localStorage, location and history with inert objects, runs it in node and then calls the model functions listed below. Mounting (rendering every panel into its section, wiring the tabs, re-rendering on state changes, loading saved data) happens in App.mount(document), called from a second, separate <script> placed after it. 4. App.store = {get(), set(patch), subscribe(fn)} holding the state {columns: [], cards: [], ui: {}}; set merges the patch into the state and notifies subscribers. App.router.show(name) makes section#panel-NAME and its tab active and hides the others. 5. App.features.NAME = {model: {...}, render(root, state)} for each of the sixteen names. render writes the feature's whole panel into root (its section) from state and wires its own events, which change state only through App.store.set. model holds pure functions: no DOM, no localStorage (persist excepted), never mutating the arrays or objects they receive, always returning new ones. DATA. A column is {id, name, wip} with wip a positive integer or null (unlimited); column order is array order. A card is {id, title, description, tags: [string], due: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or null, assignee: string or null, column: <column id>, created: 'YYYY-MM-DD', done: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or null, archived: boolean}; the order of the cards of one column is their order in the cards array. Every list function returns cards in board order. 'Active' means archived === false. Dates are compared as ISO strings; day arithmetic is whole days between two ISO dates. MODEL FUNCTIONS THE GATE CALLS, exact names and shapes: columns.model.add(columns, name) -> new array plus {id (unique), name, wip: null}; columns.model.rename(columns, id, name) -> new array; columns.model.remove(columns, id) -> new array without it; columns.model.validate(name, columns) -> array of error strings (blank after trimming; a name already used, compared case-insensitively), [] when valid. cards.model.add(cards, {title, description, tags, due, assignee, column, created}) -> new array plus the card with a unique id, done: null, archived: false; cards.model.update(cards, id, patch) -> new array with that card's named fields replaced and the others kept; cards.model.remove(cards, id) -> new array; cards.model.validate(card) -> array of error strings, one per failing rule (title blank after trimming; a tag that is not a non-empty string; due present but not YYYY-MM-DD), [] when valid. move.model.inColumn(cards, columnId) -> the active cards of that column in board order; move.model.move(cards, id, toColumnId, index) -> new array with the card in toColumnId placed at position index among that column's active cards (0 = first; an index past the end = last; moving inside its own column reorders it); every other card keeps its relative order. wiplimit.model.canMove(cards, columns, id, toColumnId) -> {ok: boolean, reason: string}: refused when the target column has a wip and already holds wip active cards not counting the card itself (so reordering inside a full column is allowed), reason a non-empty sentence when refused and '' when ok; wiplimit.model.setLimit(columns, id, wip) -> new array with that column's wip set (null lifts it). labels.model.all(cards) -> unique tags of all cards, unique and sorted case-insensitively, first spelling kept; labels.model.withTag(cards, tag) -> cards carrying the tag, compared case-insensitively; labels.model.counts(cards) -> {tag: number of cards}. search.model.search(cards, query) -> cards whose title or description contains the trimmed query case-insensitively; an empty or whitespace query returns every card. due.model.classify(card, today) -> 'none' (no due), 'overdue' (due < today), 'soon' (today <= due <= today + 3 days), 'later'; due.model.overdue(cards, today) -> active, not done cards with due < today, in board order. sortcolumn.model.sortBy(cards, columnId, key, dir) -> new array where only that column's cards are reordered by key 'due' | 'title' | 'created' (title case-insensitive) and dir 'asc' | 'desc', a missing due sorting last in both directions, every other card untouched; sortcolumn.model.inColumnOrder(cards, columnId) -> the active cards of that column in board order. archive.model.archive(cards, id), archive.model.restore(cards, id) -> new arrays toggling archived; archive.model.active(cards), archive.model.archived(cards) -> the two partitions in board order. history.model.empty() -> a fresh stack; history.model.push(stack, state) -> new stack with state on top of the past and the redo branch cleared, keeping at most 20 past states; history.model.undo(stack, current) -> {stack, state}: the most recent past state becomes state and current goes to the redo branch; with nothing to undo returns {stack, state: current}; history.model.redo(stack, current) -> {stack, state} the reverse; history.model.canUndo(stack), history.model.canRedo(stack) -> booleans; history.model.depth(stack) -> number of past states. swimlanes.model.byAssignee(cards) -> [{assignee, cards}] over active cards, one lane per assignee sorted by name, and a final lane named 'Unassigned' for cards without one, lanes with no card omitted, cards in board order. assignees.model.assign(cards, id, name), assignees.model.unassign(cards, id) -> new arrays; assignees.model.workload(cards) -> {name: number of active cards}; assignees.model.people(cards) -> sorted unique assignees of active cards. exporter.model.toJSON(state) -> a JSON string of {version: 2, columns, cards}; exporter.model.toMarkdown(state) -> one '## <column name>' heading per column in order, under it one '- [ ] <title>' line per active card of the column, '- [x] <title>' when the card has a done date, archived cards left out. importer.model.parse(text) -> {columns, cards, errors}: errors holds one string per problem (text is not JSON; no columns array; a card whose column is not in columns; a card with a blank title); cards keeps only the valid cards; a document that is not JSON or has no columns yields columns: [], cards: []. metrics.model.cycleTime(card) -> whole days from created to done, or null when not done; metrics.model.averageCycle(cards) -> the mean cycle time of every card with a done date, archived included, 0 when there is none; metrics.model.throughput(cards, weekStart) -> the number of cards whose done date lies within the seven days starting at weekStart, archived included. persist.model.KEY -> the localStorage key; persist.model.save(state) writes JSON {version: 2, columns, cards} under KEY; persist.model.load() -> the saved state {version, columns, cards} or null when nothing is stored, migrating a version-1 document first; persist.model.migrate(doc) -> a version-2 document: a version-1 document has cards carrying a `status` string instead of `column` and no columns array; migration creates one column per distinct status in order of first appearance (id derived from the name, wip null), points each card's column at it, and fills missing card fields (description '', tags [], due null, assignee null, done null, archived false); a version-2 document is returned as is.
